extracted.intended_audience: businessmen, industrialists, financiers, and young entrepreneurs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for negotiating, investing, and running industrial/manufacturing enterprises, with rules of commercial morality and specific checks for endorsements, partnerships, and capital allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity as the foundation of business
rubrics_metrics.description: A great business is seldom if ever built up, except on lines of the strictest integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation for fairness (the spirit rather than the letter of the law) is essential to permanent success. Correct errors promptly, avoid 'cuteness' or sharp dealing, and cultivate a house governed by what is fair rather than what is merely legal. Examples: Morgan repaying an extra $10,000; treating partners and clients fairly yields long-term returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always give the other party the benefit of the doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule we adopted: always give the other party the benefit of the doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This builds trust and long-term business relationships. Note: Carnegie indicates this rule excludes the speculative/gambling class and does not apply to stock gamblers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing speculation/gambling with honorable business
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock gambling and honorable business are incompatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear separation between speculative trading behavior and legitimate commercial operations; do not allow gambling atmosphere to influence firm conduct or reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-question test before endorsing commercial paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Before endorsing commercial paper ask: (1) Have I surplus means for all possible requirements which will enable me to pay without inconvenience the utmost sum for which I am liable under this endorsement? (2) Am I willing to lose this sum for the friend for whom I endorse?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if both answers are affirmative should one consider endorsing. If the first is affirmative, consider paying the whole sum immediately rather than merely endorsing. This protects creditors, family, and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit personal endorsements in partnership agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnership agreement should prevent partners from endorsing or committing themselves in any way beyond trifling sums, except for the firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal contractual limits on personal liability protect partners and families; adherence to such a rule has kept Carnegie's partners out of trouble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on and master one business
rubrics_metrics.description: The true road to preëminent success is to make yourself master in that line; put all good eggs in one basket and then watch that basket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time and capital primarily in your own business; become preeminent through focused attention and continuous reinvestment in operations and improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest surplus in first-class securities when business can't absorb it
rubrics_metrics.description: If a business will not bear extension, invest the surplus in first-class securities which will yield a moderate but certain revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than diversifying into unfamiliar enterprises, park surplus in safe, high-quality securities until a sound opportunity in your field appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage your own capital — you can often do it best
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been with me a cardinal doctrine that I could manage my own capital better than any other person, much better than any board of directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct control of capital deployment in enterprises you master; be cautious about giving others control of your invested resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep cool and patient when the other party becomes excited
rubrics_metrics.description: When one party to a bargain becomes excited, the other should keep cool and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let counterpart panic force hasty decisions. Example: in the Barings panic steady patience might have preserved a better deal; when one side is emotional, maintain composure and wait for conditions to settle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer collaboration over mutually destructive rivalry
rubrics_metrics.description: Unite with a rival rather than destroying mutual advantages (e.g., propose a joint company instead of competing propositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When competing offers would cancel each other's advantages, propose a joint arrangement to capture the opportunity cooperatively. Example: Carnegie proposed combining competing sleeping-car propositions into the Pullman Palace Car Company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give trusted partners first opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the first offer to trusted intermediaries (e.g., Junius S. Morgan) who will either buy or place the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice strengthens relationships and often ensures a willing, effective intermediary will place securities when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct internal mistakes promptly even if they favor the firm
rubrics_metrics.description: A mistake made by any one in favor of the firm is corrected as promptly as if the error were in favor of the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly rectifying favorable mistakes builds trust and reputation; the standard of commercial morality demands proactive correction of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat your means as a sacred trust for creditors while indebted
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's means are a trust to be sacredly held for his own creditors as long as he has debts and obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize obligations; avoid risking creditors' interests by imprudent endorsements or speculative commitments when indebted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate technical changes with experiments and outside expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: When facing technical difficulties (e.g., blast-furnace problems), seek expert advice and run small-scale experiments to compare alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Carnegie had model furnaces and bells built to test Whitwell's proposed bell shape; empirical trials resolved the issue. Use prototyping and external specialists rather than assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set philanthropic limits and plan before accumulation becomes an idol
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie's memorandum: secure a comfortable income (e.g., $50,000/year), then make no further effort to increase fortune but spend the surplus each year for benevolent purposes; choose a life that is elevating rather than the worship of money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide in advance a cap on personal accumulation and a plan for annual benevolence; pursue education, public influence, or philanthropic institutions rather than endless wealth accrual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid scattering investments across unrelated enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Losses men encounter which seriously embarrass them are rarely in their own business, but in enterprises of which the investor is not master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer deep investment and control in your primary line rather than spreading capital into many external concerns where you lack mastery; if diversification is necessary, choose first-class, familiar securities.
